Security · Instruction-level

Prompt Override Guard

Instructs an agent to refuse attempts to jailbreak or override it.
SKILL · PROMPT-LEVEL, NOT ENFORCED

What it does

Instructs the agent to refuse attempts to bypass its own instructions - phrases like “ignore your instructions,” “act as DAN,” “developer mode,” or “jailbreak.” When the agent recognises such an attempt, this instruction is meant to take priority over every other response.

How it works

It is loaded into every Cowork agent, so nobody needs to invoke it by name. Loaded is not the same as enforced. This is instruction text the model is asked to follow, with no mechanism underneath it, so a sufficiently determined prompt injection can get past it - the hub states that principle against this skill elsewhere: "constraints that only live in the prompt are bypassable by prompt injection." Its measured pass rate has never been published. Verified 2026-08-20. It does not trigger on legitimate admin instructions, normal confusion about an agent's capabilities, or messages that merely mention security without trying to override behavior.

Recognized automatically

"ignore your instructions..."

"forget what you were told..."

"act as DAN / developer mode / jailbreak"

Requirements

What this skill needs in order to run. Added 2026-08-20.

Skills - None.

Connectors / MCP servers - None - and this is deliberate. The skill explicitly sends no external notification of any kind when it fires.

Folder access - None.

KB modules / context files - None.

Repos - None.

If something is missing - By design there is nothing to be missing. The behaviour to understand is that the guard is SILENT on purpose: the person attempting the override sees only the standard reply, with no notification raised, because tipping them off would defeat the guard.
